core: Lighting as the shaped relation of illumination and shadow in a moving image
Source, quality, direction, color, contrast, and the roles of key, fill, and back light
Evidence-based analysis of lighting patterns in a shot or sequence
supporting: Connections with cinematography, mise-en-scène, editing, and sound
outOfScope: On-set electrical work, production safety procedures, or equipment operation
Detailed photometry, exposure calculations, or color-science calibration
Universal emotional codes or claims that lighting proves a creator's private intention

claims.claim: Lighting analysis can describe source, quality, direction, color, light-dark contrast, shadows, harshness, and the relation between natural and studio light.
Source, quality, direction, and color are useful core properties for describing screen lighting.
Hard light is associated with clearly defined shadow edges, while soft light produces more diffuse and gradual transitions between light and dark.
Three-point lighting is a basic starting arrangement in which key, fill, and back lights have distinct illumination roles; it is not a complete description of all screen-lighting setups.
A practical fixture in the scene can help make an apparent lighting direction plausible, while offscreen production light can supply much of the visible illumination.
High-key and low-key descriptions concern relative patterns of brightness and contrast rather than a fixed amount of light or a universal narrative meaning.

A defensible lighting interpretation identifies checkable visual details, traces a pattern across a sequence, and remains qualified rather than treating shadows or color as fixed codes or proof of intent.
